title: Horizon-aware microbatch orchestrator for reducing padding and improving kernel selection
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a horizon-aware microbatch orchestrator that groups requests by predicted remaining generation horizon (remaining tokens to decode) rather than raw input sequence length, enabling tighter bucketization and kernel-hint metadata so the serving runtime can select faster kernels and reduce padding during both prefill and decode phases. The goal is to reduce unnecessary padding overhead on mixed workloads (short chat turns + long generation) while preserving end-to-end latency SLOs and model output quality.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end system reduces median token padding across our mixed chat+long-gen benchmark suite by >=25% compared to current length-only bucketing baseline
Tail (p95) decode latency for short-turn workloads improves by >=15% under production traffic profile
No measurable regression (>0.5% BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity) on existing output-quality evals tied to prompt set
Kernel selection logs include hint metadata and match expected kernel families for >=95% of batches in canary
Canary rollout with traffic ramping observes no increase in error-rate or queue-overflow events
Automated fallback to length-only buckets when horizon estimator fails or runtime misses kernel hints
tasks: Prototype lightweight horizon estimator (server-side) and measure prediction latency
Design bucket key: (model_variant, predicted_horizon_quantile, prefill_flag, hardware_affinity)
Add kernel_hint field to batch descriptor and runtime API
Implement horizon-aware bucketer in request coalescer (prefill and decode paths)
Integrate with scheduler to prioritize kernel-affine batches and avoid mixing incompatible token widths
Add telemetry: padding_bytes_saved, kernel_hint_match_rate, per-batch latency breakdown
Create unit + load tests that simulate mixed chat/long-gen traffic and measure pad reduction
Prepare canary plan and dashboard for runtime-2.4 release
design_notes: Rationale: Many existing bucketers treat seqlen as static; actual cost relates to remaining decode horizon. Short-turn chat messages waste tokens when padded to long-context buckets during prefill. Estimating remaining horizon lets us group by final decode length expectation and select narrower kernels.

Horizon estimator must be lightweight: best-effort, sub-ms in hot path. Option: run estimator as part of prefill parsing step or asynchronously for streamed inputs and default to conservative estimate if missing.
Bucket granularity: use quantile-based bucketing on predicted horizon (e.g., 0-8, 9-32, 33-128, 129+ tokens) customizable per model family. Quantiles tuned per workload region.

Kernel hinting: expose kernel family preferences (e.g., fp16_fused_attn, sparse_attn_block16) as metadata attached to batch. Runtime kernel selector will consider hint + observed seq distribution when choosing kernels.
Security: ensure kernel_hint and horizon predictions do not leak sensitive information across tenants. Treat hint metadata as internal and not persisted in long-term logs without redaction.

Trade-offs: Adding estimator increases CPU work per request; mitigate by coalescing estimator calls, caching recent predictions by prompt fingerprint, and performing estimator on a sampled basis for low-cost workloads.
Fallback behavior: if estimator latency exceeds threshold or fails, fall back to current length-based bucketer to avoid blocking requests. Provide signals for operator visibility.
Compatibility: Make feature opt-in per-customer and per-model. For Dedicated/Private deployments customers can disable estimator and supply their own hinting via API.
Observability: expose new metrics and traces so we can correlate pad savings with kernel selection and latency changes. Instrument both prefill and decode phases separately.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Horizon estimator prototype + offline evaluation using 2 weeks of production traces; measure prediction accuracy vs actual remaining tokens. Phase 2: API addition for kernel_hint and bucketing key; integrate into coalescer (prefill path) and unit test. Phase 3: Scheduler changes to respect kernel affinity and prefill/decode interleaving; add telemetry and performance tests. Phase 4: Canary across small subset of traffic (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with rollback thresholds. Coordinate with runtime and telemetry teams for dashboards. Key files: coalescer/service_coalescer.go, scheduler/kernel_selector.cc, metrics/pad_savings_panel.json
testing_and_metrics: Create synthetic traffic generator that mixes 60% short chat turns (<20 remaining), 30% medium (20-100), 10% long (>100) following our production trace distribution
Measure baseline pad tokens and compare after enabling horizon bucketer: report median pad_tokens_per_request and total pad_tokens_saved
Track kernel_hint_match_rate: percentage of batches where runtime honored kernel_hint choice
Latency breakdown: prefill_latency, decode_latency, queuing_delay, kernel_switch_overhead
Quality checks: run subset of prompts through eval harness to detect hallucination/quality drift
Fault-injection tests: simulate estimator timeout, malformed hint, and ensure safe fallback
rollout_plan: Unit + integration tests green: merge to staging branch
Staging stress run at 2x baseline QPS -> validate metrics
Canary 5% traffic for 24h: monitor pad_savings, p95 latency, error-rate
Ramp to 25% for 48h if stable, then 100% with telemetry retention enabled
Post-rollout 7-day regression check and automated rollback window
Documentation: update runtime kernel selection docs, Console feature flag UI, and Playground settings
